title: Determinant laws and row operations
terms: determinant multilinearity; alternating determinant; determinant row operations; trian- gular determinant; determinant of a product; determinant scaling; determinant of a transpose.

exposition.text:
The determinant is linear in each row separately, changes sign under a row interchange, and
equals 1 at the identity. Multiplying a single row by c multiplies the determinant by c; adding
a multiple of a different row leaves it unchanged. A triangular determinant is the product of
diagonal entries.

dependent row collection gives determinant zero. The determinant is not linear in the whole
matrix, so det(A + B) is not generally det A + det B.

question.text:
A matrix B is obtained from A by swapping two rows, multiplying one row by −3, and adding
five times a row to a different row. If det B = 12, what is det A?
(A) −36 (B) −4 (C) 4 (D) 12 (E) 36

solution.text:
The net multiplier is (−1)(−3)(1) = 3. Thus 12 = 3 det A, giving 4. The row addition does
not change the determinant.

A real 5 × 5 matrix satisfies A = −A. What must its determinant be?
(A) −1
(B) 0
(C) 1
(D) A positive number
(E) Any real number is possible.

solution.text:
Transposition preserves determinant, while multiplying all five rows by −1 reverses its sign.

Thus det A = det A = det(−A) = − det A, forcing zero. Odd dimension is essential to this
argument.
